title: Hotpatch severity triage, branch strategy, and constrained backport tooling
creator: Ariel Kim
description:
Purpose: Define a prescriptive, low-latency process for triaging S0/S1 incidents, producing hotpatches, and performing constrained backports to LTS channels. This ticket codifies severity criteria, patch-branch naming and protection, automated cherry-pick tooling, minimal test/verification gates, and rollout/rollback decision thresholds for rapid remediation with controlled risk.

Scope: Applies to runtime and control-plane code that affects inference correctness, customer-facing latency/availability SLOs, and data confidentiality. Excludes purely experimental feature branches; those follow normal release cadence.

Severity taxonomy and immediate actions:
- S0 (Critical production loss / data corruption): immediate all-hands. Create hotpatch branch, bypass normal release window, owner = oncall + release lead. Target remediation window: < 60 minutes to mitigation or rollback.
- S1 (Severe degradation impacting multiple customers): prioritize hotpatch; follow expedited review within 2 hours.
- S2 (Partial degradation or feature regression with limited customers): schedule hotfix in next patch cycle unless certifiable workaround exists.
- S3 (Minor bug): backlog for next patch.

Criteria: Use quantitative signals where possible (error rate > 5% of requests, p99 latency > 3x baseline, observed data-loss or compromised outputs). If regression in quality tests or safety checks fails for a release, treat as S1 unless it causes wide availability impact.

Branching and naming conventions:
- Hotpatch branches: release/v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}-hotfix/{ENG-KEY}-{brief}
  Example: release/v2.4.1-hotfix/ENG-29486-fix-kv-cache-leak
- Patch branches must be created from the exact tag of the release being patched (not from main).
- Protect hotpatch branches: require 2 reviewers, CI green, and "hotpatch" label on PR.
- Backport targets: LTS channels are explicit branches: release/v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}-lts, release/v{MAJOR-1}.{MINOR}-lts where maintained. Backport only if patch meets acceptance criteria in "Backport policy" below.

Backport policy and constrained cherry-picks:
- Backport only corrections that are low-risk (no large refactors, no new feature flags, no config schema changes).
- Mandatory checklist for backport PRs: unit tests, regression tests for the failing path, smoke deploy to canary cluster.
- Use the rwd-backport tool to generate cherry-pick candidates and create draft PRs. Draft PRs must reference source hotpatch PR and include the backport checklist.
- If the backport applies to multiple LTS branches, create one PR per target branch. Label with "backport-needed" and list the source commit SHA.

Automated tooling and CI gates:
- rwd-backport: CLI that attempts cherry-picks, runs a quick build/test matrix, and opens draft PRs. It has a --dry-run mode and a --preserve-commit-author flag.
- CI gating: hotpatch PRs must pass the "hotpatch" matrix: unit, quick-integration (targeted subset), smoke-deploy. Full integration suite is optional before canary but required before full rollout.
- Canary deploy automation: rolling canary jobs orchestrated by the deployer pipeline. Canary percent steps: 1%, 5%, 25%, 100% with observation windows (default 30 minutes at 1% and 5%, 60 minutes at 25%). These windows are configurable per-release.

Rollout decision criteria and rollback triggers:
- Advance canary if: error rate <= 2x baseline, p99 latency ≤ baseline + 100ms, automated output quality checks pass.
- Abort and rollback if: error rate > 3x baseline for 5 minutes, increase in p99 latency > 150ms sustained for 5 minutes, or output regression tests fail.
- Rollback action: immediate revert to previous stable tag via the orchestrator and remove hotpatch branch-only traffic. Document revert commit and trigger postmortem.

Post-deploy verification and communications:
- Release lead must post a canary health summary to #release-updates after each canary step (template provided in attachments).
- If backport is required, attach backport PR links and estimated timeline to customer-impact incident report.

PR and review checklist (to be present in PR body):
- Source commit SHA and reason for hotpatch.
- Tests added/updated and their scope.
- Minimal risk statement (why safe to backport).
- Rollout plan with canary percentages and rollback thresholds.
- Link to incident/investigation doc.

Escalation and ownership:
- Owner = oncall engineer + release lead. If security-sensitive, also assign Security lead.
- Pager escalation: oncall -> release lead -> VP Eng.

Observability changes required as part of hotpatch PRs (where applicable):
- Add a short-lived metric for the fixed code path to ensure observed coverage during canary.
- If changing cache behavior, add KV cache hit/miss and memory delta metrics to the canary dashboard.

Operational runbook fragments and sample commands:
- Create hotpatch branch: git checkout -b release/v2.4.1-hotfix/ENG-29486-fix-kv-cache-leak v2.4.1
- Create hotpatch PR: hub pull-request -b release/v2.4.1-hotfix -l hotpatch -m "HOTPATCH: ENG-29486 - kv cache leak fix"
- Run backport tool: rwd-backport --source-commit {SHA} --targets release/v2.4-lts,release/v2.3-lts --create-draft

Conformance and metrics we will track:
- Time-to-mitigate for S0/S1 incidents (goal: median < 90 minutes).
- Mean time from hotpatch PR open to canary (goal: < 120 minutes).
- Backport success rate (goal: 95% automated cherry-picks).

Decision notes: We deliberately require a stricter review and canary cadence for hotpatches to balance risk vs speed. Security-reviewed hotpatches that touch crypto/KMS surfaces must include security sign-off before full rollout.

Links to artifacts and runbooks are in attachments. The goal is an auditable, repeatable hotpatch lifecycle that minimizes blast radius while restoring customer SLOs quickly.
